note.text: Correlative conjunctions work in pairs: both ... and, either ... or, neither ... nor and not only ... but also. They join parallel structures and express different relationships. Both includes the alternatives; either offers an alternative; neither excludes them. Put the pair around matching grammatical units. Subject-verb agreement can become complex when subjects differ, so the introductory examples use unambiguous pairs. Do not combine either with nor or use a negative pair as if it meant both.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: Both Bih and Ayuk joined the club includes them. Neither Bih nor Ayuk was absent excludes each from the absence claim. The club can meet either indoors or outdoors presents alternatives. Not only reading but also discussion names related activities. Keep the same kind of structure on each side of a pair.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Choose the relationship before filling a pair. Check that nouns join nouns or corresponding phrases join corresponding phrases. Read the complete sentence to avoid an unintended double negative. More complex mixed-number agreement should be checked with the teacher's course convention.
